new_findings.text: hunter-s27b/heavy-reach-has-a-hard-100px-floor records its one remaining unknown as 'the base value §1t4420s0§ ... which is set elsewhere and which I did not resolve'. It resolves. Web: §1t99s0§.as:105 initialises §1t4420s0§ to 10, :194 assigns it from the tenth initPlayer parameter, and :223 halves it ('*= 0.5') in one branch. The android twin is positionally identical - MCSPlayer.as:107 'internal var baseSlashLength:int = 10;', :182 declares initPlayer with baseSlashLength as its tenth parameter, :193 assigns it, :222 halves it - which names §1t4420s0§ = baseSlashLength. The value fed in, for NPCs, is computed by the caller: EnemyElite.as:102 baseSlashLength = 120 + floor(90 * speed / (20 + speed)), i.e. a saturating curve from 120 px at speed 0 toward 210 px, 165 px at speed 20. So reach = baseSlashLength x per-stance multiplier, and at the low end the 100 px heavy floor genuinely bites: base 120 at mastery 0 gives 120 x 0.5 = 60, clamped up to 100. CAVEAT, stated plainly: the formula line is android v0.682, so under S0-3/C2 it is v0.682 until a web caller is read; what IS web-attested is that the base is an injected per-fighter slash length with a halving branch, not a global constant. Two further web stance cases the original finding did not list: §1t99s0§.as:3131 (Dual) = base * 1.4 and :3142 (Reversed) = base * 1.0.

The player's baseSlashLength comes from the equivalent web caller and is still unread - that is now the ONLY missing number for reach, and it is one lookup, not a measurement.

The real count is TWENTY-SIX of 158, and the seven named are simply the first seven in document order. The full list: heavyhorizontalslash_partc (4 empty of 7 frames), balancedhorizontalslash_partc (2/7), balancedjumpslash_parta (2/7), sheathesword (2/7), backstep (2/16), forwardstep (10/16), katanajump (2/4), spearbowjump (2/4), downedup (2/4), downstab_up (7/10), downedup2 (2/25), gangnam (44/88), jutsu_ground_parta (6/9), jutsu_punch_parta (4/5), jutsu_blow_parta (4/8), jutsu_blow_partb (15/18), stomp_parta (5/10), punchcombo_parta (3/5), punchcombo_partb (4/6), punchcombo_partc (3/7), punchcombo_partd (8/12), narutorun (6/12), sheathesword3 (22/33), jutsu_air (5/10), punchground_parta (4/7), punchground_partb (13/16). This enlarges the renderer risk rather than changing its direction: 16% of the human clips contain frames that key NOTHING, and in gangnam and sheathesword3 the empty frames are the majority. A renderer that resets unlisted joints per frame does not merely tear the corpse apart on dismemberment tails - it blanks the character outright for half of two long clips. Carry-forward-last-transform is mandatory, not an optimisation.
new_findings.lane_impact: L6 art-anim: the animation player MUST hold the last written transform for every joint not listed in the current frame, and an empty <f> is a legal hold-frame (a timing beat), not a corrupt row to skip. Do not 'repair' empty frames in the importer.
